ponge.title: Connes’ integration and Weyl’s laws
ponge.proposition_or_scope: Theorem 6.12 on printed pp. 752–753 states Birman–Solomyak's compact-support Euclidean negative-order pseudodifferential Weyl laws. Signed eigenvalue asymptotics (6.13) require self-adjointness and use the signed principal symbol. Applying it to a sharply compressed scalar Helmholtz kernel requires the separate cutoff and lower-order remainder argument. This continuum result supplies no finite-grid inertia equality.
ponge.bibliographic_note: Publisher reports 28 April 2023; Crossref date parts show 27 April. Both give 2023 and identical issue/pages.

douglas.title: On majorization, factorization, and range inclusion of operators on Hilbert space
douglas.journal: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society
douglas.proposition_or_scope: Theorem 1, pp. 413–414, equates range inclusion, AA* ≤ λ² BB*, and A=BC with bounded C. The reduced solution has minimum factor norm and range in the closure of ran(B*). The author's Added in proof explicitly allows different source Hilbert spaces with a common target. That extension covers the finite rectangular Gram/range application.

fan.title: On a Theorem of Weyl Concerning Eigenvalues of Linear Transformations I
fan.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
fan.proposition_or_scope: Theorem 1, printed p. 653, identifies the maximum/minimum trace on q orthonormal vectors with sums of the largest/smallest q eigenvalues, respectively, for a Hermitian operator. The manuscript applies the variational principle to source spectral sums. Its rank restrictions and full-box conclusions are separate derivations.

millerabs.title: Fundamental limits to optical response in absorptive systems
millerabs.proposition_or_scope: Section 2 and equations (4), (5) give absorbed power as a dissipative quadratic and extinction as a linear functional of polarization currents. Section 3.2 equation (30) specializes the material factor to |χ|²/Im χ. This supports the loss-limited current scale for strictly absorptive material. Vacuum and the lossless endpoint require the stated discrete material assumptions and proof.
millerabs.bibliographic_note: The Optica Crossref deposit lists the first page only. The printed PDF confirms 3329–3364. Electronic publication is 9 February 2016 and the issue is dated 22 February 2016.
